spinophorosaurus:enwiki:8.title: Spinophorosaurus (Girdles, limbs, and misidentified tail spikes)

facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: genus: Spinophorosaurus

facts.statement: The species name is nigerensis.
facts.quote: species: nigerensis

facts.statement: The genus and species were described by Remes et al. in 2009.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Remes et al., 2009

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Middle Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Jurassic,

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus is a sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day Niger during the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Niger during the Middle Jurassic period.

facts.statement: The first skeleton was designated the holotype specimen of Spinophorosaurus nigerensis in 2009.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis in 2009

facts.statement: The generic name means "spine-bearing lizard" and originally referred to what were thought to be spiked osteoderms.
facts.quote: The generic name ("spine-bearing lizard") refers to what was initially thought to be spiked osteoderms

facts.statement: The specific name refers to the location where the animal was found.
facts.quote: The specific name (Niger and -ensis) refers to where it was found.

facts.statement: The subadult holotype specimen was estimated to be around 13 meters in length.
facts.quote: The subadult holotype specimen is estimated to have been around 13 m in length

facts.statement: The paratype specimen was estimated to be about 14 meters long.
facts.quote: whereas the paratype was about 14 m long.

facts.statement: The shoulder height of these individuals was estimated at around 4 meters.
facts.quote: The shoulder height reached by these individuals was estimated at around 4 m

facts.statement: The weight of these individuals was estimated at about 7 metric tons.
facts.quote: and the weight at about 7 MT.

facts.statement: Bones on the tail tip originally thought to be spiked osteoderms were later suggested to be clavicles.
facts.quote: Bones originally thought to be osteoderms bearing spikes placed on the tail tip were later suggested to be clavicles.

facts.statement: One study suggests Spinophorosaurus may have been a high browser.
facts.quote: One study suggests it may have been a high browser

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus is known from the Irhazer Shale, a geological formation thought to be Middle Jurassic in age.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus is known from the Irhazer Shale, a geological formation thought to be Middle Jurassic in age.

facts.statement: German explorers Ulrich Joger and Edgar Sommer explored the semi-deserts south of Agadez in early 2005.
facts.quote: Early in 2005, German explorers Ulrich Joger and Edgar Sommer explored the semi-deserts south of Agadez

facts.statement: Ulrich Joger discovered a complete femur that became the holotype specimen of Spinophorosaurus after a one-hour search.
facts.quote: After a one-hour search, Joger discovered a rounded bone tip sticking out of the surface, which after further excavation turned out to be a complete femur (thigh bone) of what would later become the holotype specimen of Spinophorosaurus.

facts.statement: Joger and Sommer uncovered most of the holotype specimen with the help of local Tuaregs after two days.
facts.quote: Joger and Sommer then hired local Tuaregs for support and, after two days, had uncovered most of the specimen

facts.statement: The official excavation campaign, dubbed "Projekt Dino", started on March 1, 2007.
facts.quote: The official campaign, dubbed "Projekt Dino", started on 1 March 2007

facts.statement: The German team discovered the second specimen, the future paratype, 15 meters from the first on March 17.
facts.quote: the German team discovered a second Spinophorosaurus specimen, the future paratype, 15 m apart from the first, on 17 March.

facts.statement: Excavation was usually interrupted between 12:00 and 15:00 when temperatures reached 43 to 45 degrees Celsius.
facts.quote: Excavation was usually interrupted between 12:00 and 15:00 when temperatures reached 43 – 45 °C.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Spinophorosaurus is a very basal sauropod or belongs inside Eusauropoda.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus has been classified as either a very basal sauropod, or inside Eusauropoda, a more derived group.

facts.statement: Excavation of the fossils was completed on April 2, and they were transported to the port of Cotonou on April 3.
facts.quote: Excavation was completed on 2 April, and the fossils were packed for transport to the port of Cotonou on 3 April.

facts.statement: German paleontologist Kristian Remes and colleagues described the species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis in 2009 using a holotype specimen split between the Elche and Braunschweig museums.
facts.quote: The first skeleton (divided between the Elche museum, where it was catalogued as GCP-CV-4229, and the Braunschweig museum, catalogued as NMB-1699-R) was made the holotype of the new genus and species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis by German palaeontologist Kristian Remes and colleagues of the German and Spanish teams in 2009.

facts.statement: The generic name means "spine-bearing lizard" and originally referred to structures thought to be spiked osteoderms, though they were later suggested to be clavicles.
facts.quote: The generic name is composed of spina, Latin for "spike"; , Greek for "to bear"; and sauros, which means lizard ("spine-bearing lizard" in full): the name refers to what was initially interpreted as osteoderms bearing spikes, which were later suggested to represent clavicles instead.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes a nearly complete postcranial skeleton, a braincase, and several skull bones, but lacks the sternum, forelimb, and foot.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen consists of a braincase, a postorbital bone, a squamosal, a quadrate, a pterygoid, a surangular, and a nearly complete postcranial skeleton, which lacks the sternum, antebrachium, manus, and pes.

facts.statement: A small sauropod skeleton was discovered near the two main Spinophorosaurus specimens in 2012.
facts.quote: In 2012, Adrián Páramo and Francisco Ortega from the PALDES team reported a small sauropod skeleton (specimen GCP-CV-BB-15) that had been discovered on the ground, a few metres from the two Spinophorosaurus specimens

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the small skeleton found nearby likely represents a juvenile Spinophorosaurus, with differences explained by growth.
facts.quote: Several distinct features of the skeleton are shared with Spinophorosaurus, and though some features of that genus are not present, it most likely represents a juvenile Spinophorosaurus (the differences probably explained by ontogeny, changes during growth).

facts.statement: The holotype was initially estimated to be 13 meters long, while the paratype was estimated to be 14 meters long.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was initially estimated to have been around 13 m in length when measured along the vertebral column, while the paratype was about 13 per cent larger, measuring around 14 m.

facts.statement: A later 3D photogrammetry model measured the holotype skeleton at 11.7 meters from head to tail.
facts.quote: A later 3D photogrammetry model of the holotype skeleton measures 11.7 m from head to tail

facts.statement: In 2023, the holotype was listed as 11 meters long, the paratype as 13 meters, and the juvenile as 3 meters.
facts.quote: In 2023, Vidal listed the holotype as 11 m long, the paratype as 13 m, and the juvenile as 3 m.

facts.statement: The shoulder height of these individuals was estimated at around 4 meters and the weight at about 7 metric tons.
facts.quote: The shoulder height reached by these individuals was estimated at around 4 m, and the weight at about 7 MT.

facts.statement: The holotype had unfused sutures indicating it was a subadult, while the paratype had fully fused sutures.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen's endocranial and neurocentral sutures in the skull and vertebrae respectively are unfused, indicating it was a subadult, whereas the paratype specimen has fully fused neurocentral sutures.

facts.statement: The frontal bones of the Spinophorosaurus skull roof were fused along the midline, a feature distinct from other skull sutures.
facts.quote: The frontal bones of the skull roof were fused in the midline, unlike the other sutures of the skull.

facts.statement: A small pineal foramen located approximately 10 mm in front of the frontal-parietal suture was present between the frontal bones of the skull.
facts.quote: Between the frontals was a small pineal foramen, about 10 mm in front of the suture between the frontal and the parietal bones.

facts.statement: The rear margin of the Spinophorosaurus skull possessed an open postparietal notch, a trait otherwise found only in dicraeosaurids and Abrosaurus.
facts.quote: The rear margin of the skull had an open postparietal notch, a feature otherwise only known in dicraeosaurids and Abrosaurus.

facts.statement: The occipital condyle at the back of the Spinophorosaurus skull was concave on the sides, similar to that of Shunosaurus.
facts.quote: The occipital condyle at the back of the skull was concave on the sides, like in Shunosaurus.

facts.statement: The basal tubera of the Spinophorosaurus skull base were enlarged and directed to the sides, a feature unique among known sauropods.
facts.quote: The basal tubera (a pair of extensions on the underside of the skull base that served as muscle attachments) were enlarged and were directed to the sides, unique among known sauropods.

facts.statement: The spatulate teeth of Spinophorosaurus were unique in having enlarged, spaced denticles around the crown top with a higher count on the front edge.
facts.quote: The spatulate (spoon shaped) teeth were unique in possessing enlarged, spaced denticles around the top of the crown, with a higher count of denticles on the front edge of the crown.

facts.statement: The neck of Spinophorosaurus was composed of 13 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: The neck was composed of 13 cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: The trunk of Spinophorosaurus consisted of 12 dorsal vertebrae and four sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: The trunk had 12 dorsal and four sacral vertebrae.

facts.statement: The tail of Spinophorosaurus comprised more than 37 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The tail comprised more than 37 caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The cervical centra of Spinophorosaurus featured large excavations on their sides that deepened toward the front, known as pleurocoels, which were also developed in Jobaria and Patagosaurus.
facts.quote: The cervical centra had large excavations on their sides that deepened towards the front; such pleurocoels were also developed in Jobaria and Patagosaurus.

facts.statement: A U-shaped depression between the centrum and neural arch in side view is an autapomorphy, or unique feature, of Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: In side view, a U-shaped depression was present between the centrum and the neural arch, which is an autapomorphy (unique feature) of Spinophorosaurus.

facts.statement: The Spinophorosaurus ribcage can be clearly subdivided into pectoral and lumbar sections, a differentiation described in only one other sauropod, the dicraeosaurid Brachytrachelopan.
facts.quote: The ribcage can therefore be clearly subdivided into a pectoral and a lumbar section; such a differentiation has only been described in a single other sauropod, the dicraeosaurid Brachytrachelopan.

facts.statement: The scapula of Spinophorosaurus was D-shaped in cross-section, a feature characteristic of eusauropods.
facts.quote: It was D-shaped in cross-section, a feature characteristic for eusauropods.

facts.statement: The coracoid of Spinophorosaurus had a distinct kidney-shape considered an autapomorphy.
facts.quote: The coracoid, which articulated to the lower end of the scapula, showed a distinct kidney-shape, considered an autapomorphy.

facts.statement: The fourth trochanter of the femur was especially large in Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: The fourth trochanter, which projected from the back surface and anchored muscles that drew the hind leg backwards, was especially large in Spinophorosaurus.

facts.statement: A large opening near the fourth trochanter, absent in other sauropods, is an autapomorphy of Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: Close to the fourth trochanter was a large opening that is absent in other sauropods, and thus an autapomorphy.

facts.statement: Elements originally interpreted as osteoderms were found with the holotype skeleton of Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: Elements originally interpreted as a left and right osteoderm (bone formed in the skin) were found with the holotype skeleton.

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis is the only known species in the extinct genus Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Spinophorosaurus

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis is a sauropod dinosaur of the saurischian type.
facts.quote: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Spinophorosaurus (del lat.+gr. «lagarto portador de espinas») de dinosaurio saurisquio saurópodo

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus lived approximately 167 million years ago during the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 167 millones de años durante el Bathoniense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The type species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis is one of the most complete basal sauropod specimens recovered to date.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de este género, Spinophorosaurus nigerensis, es uno de los ejemplares de saurópodo basales más completos recuperados hasta ahora

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus nigerensis is the first of its type found on the African continent.
facts.quote: además de ser el primero de su tipo hallado en el continente africano.

facts.statement: The genus Spinophorosaurus was named by Remes et al. in 2009.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Remes et al., 2009

facts.statement: The species Spinophorosaurus nigerensis was named by Remes et al. in 2009.
facts.quote: species_authority: Remes et al., 2009

facts.statement: In 2013, researchers reexamined supposed tail spikes in Spinophorosaurus and found they lacked the typical rugose surface of osteoderms or the club-like expansion seen in Shunosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2013, palaeontologists Emanuel Tschopp and Octávio Mateus reexamined the supposed tail spikes and found they did not have the typical rugose surface of osteoderms seen in other armoured dinosaurs, or the club-like expansion seen in Shunosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers doubted whether the supposed tail spikes were of different sizes as originally proposed due to their broken edges.
facts.quote: Due to their broken edges, They also doubted whether these elements were of different sizes as originally proposed.

facts.statement: Several subsequent studies suggested a basal position outside Eusauropoda, placing Spinophorosaurus as the sister taxon of Tazoudasaurus or Volkheimeria.
facts.quote: A similarly basal position outside of Eusauropoda was suggested by several subsequent studies, which placed Spinophorosaurus as the sister taxon of Tazoudasaurus or Volkheimeria.

facts.statement: In 2013, Pedro Mocho and colleagues argued that Spinophorosaurus was nested within eusauropods based on newly prepared bones.
facts.quote: In a 2013 conference abstract, palaeontologist Pedro Mocho and colleagues re-evaluated the phylogenetic relationships of the genus by incorporating further information from newly prepared bones, arguing that Spinophorosaurus was nested within eusauropods.

facts.statement: A 2015 study proposed a more derived position within Eusauropoda, finding Spinophorosaurus to be the sister taxon of Nebulasaurus.
facts.quote: A much more derived systematic position within Eusauropoda was also proposed by a 2015 study, which found Spinophorosaurus to be the sister taxon of Nebulasaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was approximately 13 meters long when measured along the vertebral column.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo tenía alrededor de 13 metros de largo cuando se mide a lo largo de la columna vertebral

facts.statement: The paratype was approximately 13 percent larger, measuring around 14 meters.
facts.quote: el paratipo era aproximadamente un 13 por ciento más grande, midiendo alrededor de 14 metros

facts.statement: A 3D photogrammetry model of the holotype skeleton measures 11.7 meters from head to tail.
facts.quote: Un modelo de fotogrametría 3D del esqueleto holotipo mide 11,7 metros de la cabeza a la cola

facts.statement: The shoulder height of these individuals was estimated to be around 4 meters.
facts.quote: La altura de los hombros alcanzada por estos individuos se estimó en alrededor de 4 metros

facts.statement: The weight was estimated to be around 7 tonnes.
facts.quote: y el peso en alrededor de 7 toneladas

facts.statement: The holotype had unfused endocranial and neurocentral sutures in the skull and vertebrae, respectively, indicating it was a subadult.
facts.quote: Las suturas endocraneales y neurocentrales del espécimen holotipo en el cráneo y las vértebras, respectivamente, no están fusionados, lo que indica que era un subadulto

facts.statement: The paratype specimen has completely fused neurocentral sutures.
facts.quote: el espécimen paratipo tiene suturas neurocentrales completamente fusionadas

facts.statement: The snout of the Spinophorosaurus would have been held about 5 meters above the ground.
facts.quote: el hocico del Spinophorosaurus se habría sostenido a unos 5 metros sobre el suelo

facts.statement: The acetabulum where the hind leg joined the pelvis was at a height of 2.15 meters.
facts.quote: el acetábulo donde la pata trasera se unía a la pelvis, que estaban a una altura de 2,15 metros

facts.statement: There was a small pineal foramen between the frontals, about 10 millimeters in front of the suture between the frontal and parietal bones.
facts.quote: Entre los frontales había un pequeño agujero pineal , a unos 10 milímetros por delante de la sutura entre el frontal y los huesos parietales

facts.statement: The posterior margin of the skull had an open postparietal notch, a feature otherwise known only in dicraeosaurs and Abrosaurus.
facts.quote: El margen posterior del cráneo tenía una muesca postparietal abierta, una característica que de otro modo solo se conoce en dicreosáuridos y Abrosaurus

facts.statement: The upper temporal windows, a pair of main openings in the roof of the skull, were four times wider than they were long.
facts.quote: Las ventanas temporales superiores, un par de aberturas principales en el techo del cráneo, eran cuatro veces más anchas que largas

facts.statement: The spatulate, spoon-shaped teeth were the only ones possessing enlarged and spaced denticles around the upper part of the crown.
facts.quote: Los dientes espatulados, en forma de cuchara, eran los únicos que poseían dentículos agrandados y espaciados alrededor de la parte superior de la corona

facts.statement: The inner ear labyrinth was characterized by long and thin semicircular canals, similar to those of Massospondylus and Giraffatitan.
facts.quote: El laberinto del oído interno se caracterizaba por tener canales semicirculares largos y delgados , similares a los de Massospondylus y Giraffatitan

facts.statement: The parent group of Spinophorosaurus is Gravisauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gravisauria

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.

facts.statement: Spinophorosaurus lived from the Bajocian to the Bathonian stages, between 170.9 and 165.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bathonian (170.9 to 165.3 million years ago)
